subsystems.name: Program interface and IR
subsystems.role: expresses the workload as a parameterised circuit plus a classical update rule, in a portable form.
parts: classical update function or cost function

subsystems.name: Compiler and transpiler
subsystems.role: rewrites the abstract circuit into operations the chosen device can actually run.
parts: gate decomposition to native gate set
qubit routing against the device coupling map

subsystems.name: Classical optimiser loop
subsystems.role: computes the next set of circuit parameters from measured results.
parts: gradient-free optimisers such as COBYLA or SPSA

subsystems.name: Runtime, session and scheduler
subsystems.role: turns a hybrid program into queued jobs against live hardware and reserves classical resources alongside.

subsystems.name: QPU control stack
subsystems.role: executes the compiled circuit as timed control signals and reads back the results.

subsystems.name: Error mitigation and correction
subsystems.role: improves the answer given today's noisy hardware, and later protects logical qubits.
parts: zero-noise extrapolation and probabilistic error cancellation
for error correction: syndrome extraction and a decoder

subsystems.name: Results, provenance and telemetry
subsystems.role: streams values back, records what device and calibration produced them, and checkpoints the run.

buildSteps.title: Define the hybrid program
buildSteps.detail: Write the workload as a parameterised circuit plus a classical cost function, declaring how many shots each iteration needs and how parameters will be updated.

buildSteps.title: Lower to an intermediate representation
buildSteps.detail: Compile the abstract description into a stable IR such as OpenQASM 3 or QIR so it can target more than one vendor's stack.

buildSteps.title: Compile for a specific device
buildSteps.detail: Transpile to the native gate set, route two-qubit gates onto working couplers, and pick a qubit layout suited to the device's current error rates.

buildSteps.title: Open a session and schedule
buildSteps.detail: Submit the program as a session or hybrid job so that repeated iterations keep priority on one machine and get classical workers reserved next to it.

buildSteps.title: Run the quantum inner step
buildSteps.detail: The control stack plays out the circuit, performs mid-circuit measurement where needed, and returns measurement counts for each shot.

buildSteps.title: Compute classically between shots
buildSteps.detail: Expectation values are formed from the counts, the optimiser proposes new parameters, and the next circuit is prepared — the loop that gives the approach its name.

buildSteps.title: Apply mitigation every iteration
buildSteps.detail: Readout calibration, noise extrapolation or cancellation is applied per iteration, since a single mitigated number cannot be built from separately mitigated steps.

buildSteps.title: Iterate and checkpoint
buildSteps.detail: Repeat until the optimiser converges or the shot/time budget is exhausted, checkpointing parameters and device state so a long run can survive a queue interruption.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and report results
buildSteps.detail: Return estimates with error bars, tagging them with the device, calibration snapshot and software versions that produced them.

prerequisites.tech: Cloud-accessible quantum processors with stable job APIs
prerequisites.why: orchestration only has something to orchestrate once hardware is reachable programmatically.
the split into a quantum circuit and a classical optimiser is what the middleware is built around.
they make near-term results usable but cost extra shots and only hold for certain noise models.

prerequisites.tech: Standard intermediate representations and gate-model portability
prerequisites.why: without a common IR every workload must be rewritten per vendor.

prerequisites.tech: Low-latency classical control of quantum hardware
prerequisites.why: error-corrected logical qubits need feedback within roughly a microsecond, far faster than today's job-level scheduling.

pathway.milestone: runtime services offering estimator/sampler primitives with built-in mitigation and session-based job batches
pathway.unlocks: variational algorithms and chemistry or optimisation experiments run end-to-end without hand-written glue code.

pathway.milestone: standardised hybrid intermediate representations and pulse-level control APIs
pathway.unlocks: the same program ported across vendors and across circuit-level versus pulse-level execution.

pathway.milestone: real-time feedback at scale: repeated mid-circuit measurement, reset and conditional operations inside one job
pathway.unlocks: error correction experiments and deeper circuits than a single coherent run allows.

pathway.milestone: microsecond-scale decoding and control planes coupled to error-corrected logical qubits
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant workloads, where orchestration becomes a hard real-time control problem rather than a job queue.
